desc:
Usage-based billing for seats, credits and metered plans, built by Ecom Swift LLC. We record usage in your app, send it to your billing provider, show customers a live meter and produce invoices that explain every charge.

## What is usage-based billing?

Usage-based billing charges customers according to what they use instead of a flat monthly fee. There are three common forms. Per-seat billing charges for each team member. Metered billing charges for a measured action, such as API calls, exports or messages. Credit billing lets customers buy a balance in advance and spend it as they use the product.

Many products combine these with a flat base: a plan includes a set amount, and anything beyond it is billed as overage. The idea is simple. The engineering is not, because every counted event must be accurate and every invoice must be explainable.

## Why accurate metering protects trust

Customers accept variable bills only when they can understand them. A product that charges for usage but shows no meter feels risky, since the customer cannot tell what the month will cost. A bill with an unexplained number leads to a support ticket, and a wrong number leads to a refund and a lost customer.

Done well, the model is fair to both sides. Small customers pay little, large customers pay more as they get more value, and your revenue grows with their success. Visible meters, alerts before limits and optional spending caps turn the model into something customers can plan around. Billing errors are mostly counting errors, so the focus is on recording each event once and only once.

## What a good usage billing setup includes

- Usage events recorded by your app at the moment they happen.
- Events sent to the billing provider with a unique identifier, so repeats are not counted twice.
- A meter defined for each billable action, with a clear unit.
- An included amount in each plan, plus a price for overage.
- Per-seat counts synced to billing, adjusting when members join or leave.
- A prepaid credit balance with a top-up flow and a spend-down record.
- A live usage display in the customer dashboard.
- Alerts when a customer approaches and reaches an included limit.
- An optional spending cap for each customer.
- Invoice lines that name the meter, the quantity and the price per unit.

## How we work

We start by agreeing what is billable and how it is counted. Then we add event recording to your app, connect it to the meters in your provider and test with sample usage across a full billing period. The Basic package covers per-seat billing: a seat price, seat counts synced to billing, charges that adjust as seats change and a seat limit shown in the app. The Standard package adds one usage meter with events from your app, a usage display in the customer dashboard, an included amount with an overage price and a test month. The Premium package supports several meters or a credit balance, prepaid top-ups, alerts, an optional spending cap and a handover call.

We test the numbers by sending known quantities and comparing them to the invoice, line by line. Providers differ in how they support metering, so we confirm that yours can handle the model before work begins. If your product is not yet live, we can build and test against sample data.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose one clear unit for each meter that customers already understand.
- Give every usage event a unique identifier.
- Show current usage inside the product, not only on the invoice.
- Send an alert before a customer reaches a limit.
- Offer a spending cap for customers who want certainty.

**Avoid:**
- Billing for something customers cannot see or measure themselves.
- Counting events in two places that can disagree.
- Changing the meaning of a unit after customers have started.
- Sending a first overage bill without any earlier warning.
- Launching without a test month of sample usage.

## Who this suits

This service suits a developer tool or API product that charges by call volume. It suits a team product that prices by seat and needs charges to follow membership changes. It also suits an app that sells credits for exports, messages or generated items and needs a clean balance.

## What we need and how to begin

Tell us what you want to charge for, which provider you use and where in your app each billable action happens. Send any pricing notes you have, even rough ones. We need developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account, and we never need passwords. After ordering, you receive a short checklist and a test report showing sample usage against the resulting invoice.
